name: Fort Collins
seat: Fort Collins (home-rule city in Larimer County)

officials.name: Emily Francis
officials.note: Sworn in January 2026 (won the November 2025 ranked-choice election).

quorum_court.source: Fort Collins is a home-rule, council-manager city: an elected Mayor and six district councilmembers set policy, and a professional City Manager runs operations. It sits in Larimer County.

budget_adoption_window.note: The city adopts a biennial budget by ordinance in the fall; the fiscal year is the calendar year.

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues.

election_office.name: Larimer County Clerk & Recorder — Elections
election_office.address: 200 W. Oak St., Suite 5100, Fort Collins
election_office.early_voting: Larimer County has 24 ballot boxes, open 24 hours a day since Oct. 2. Its 21 vote centers open in stages from Oct. 19 to Nov. 2. In Fort Collins, the first two open Oct. 19: Larimer County Administrative Services (200 W. Oak St.) and the CSU Lory Student Center. Vote centers are open 8 am to 5 pm on weekdays and on Saturday, Oct. 31. The county lists every site at https://www.larimer.gov/clerk/elections/where-to-vote.
election_office.election_day: Vote centers are open 7 am to 7 pm. Ballots must reach the county by 7 pm. Postmarks do not count. Find a site at https://www.larimer.gov/clerk/elections/where-to-vote.
